hero.title: Ship the product, not the plumbing
hero.subtitle: Accounts, organizations, billing and an admin console are already built and already tested. Start where the interesting work is.

highlights.heading: What you start with
highlights.accounts_body: Sign-up, sessions, two-factor authentication, invitations and per-organization roles, isolated by tenant from the first query.
highlights.billing_body: Plans, trials, upgrades and dunning, with webhook handling that stays correct when the same event arrives twice.
highlights.operations_body: Structured logs, metrics, audit trails and runbooks, so the first incident is something you read about rather than guess at.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: Everything below is implemented, tested and switchable. Turn a module off and its routes, its tables and its interface go with it.
features.accounts_body: Password and OAuth sign-in, email verification, session revocation, recovery codes and step-up authentication for the actions that deserve it.
features.teams_body: Multi-organization membership, invitations, per-organization permissions, and tenant isolation enforced in the query layer rather than remembered by each endpoint.
features.billing_title: Billing that survives a webhook storm
features.billing_body: Stripe checkout, the customer portal, plan limits, trials and a dunning sequence — all idempotent, because the same event will arrive twice.
features.files_body: S3-compatible uploads with presigned URLs, scanned and size-limited, wired to the same permission model as everything else.
features.i18n_title: Six locales, one source of truth
features.i18n_body: The product, the emails and this marketing site read the same translation files, so a term cannot mean one thing in the app and another on the pricing page.
features.operations_title: Operations you do not have to invent
features.operations_body: Structured logging, Prometheus metrics, audit trails, backup and key-rotation runbooks, load tests and an accessibility gate in the pipeline.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.subtitle: Every plan includes the whole platform. What changes is how much of it you use.
pricing.committed_notice: These prices were published with the site and change on the next deploy, not the next database update.

starting_point.question: Is this a framework or a starting point?
starting_point.answer: A starting point. You get the repository and you own every line in it — the modules are ordinary code you can read, change or delete, and nothing calls home at runtime.

modules.question: Can I remove the parts I do not need?
modules.answer: Yes. Each optional module is one switch in one configuration file, and turning it off takes its routes, its database tables and its interface with it — not just the menu entry that led there.

stack.question: What is it built on?
stack.answer: A FastAPI and PostgreSQL backend, a React and TypeScript web app, and a shared component and translation layer that both of them read from. No wrapper you cannot open.

no_card.question: Do I need a card to start?
no_card.answer: No. The free plan asks for no payment details, and you only see a checkout when you choose a paid plan.

change_plan.question: Can I change plan later?
change_plan.answer: At any time, from the billing portal. An upgrade applies immediately, and what you have already paid is prorated against it.

trial.question: Is there a trial?
trial.answer: A paid plan can carry a trial period: you get the whole plan, you are not charged while it runs, and you are emailed before it ends rather than after.

payment.question: How is payment handled?
payment.answer: Through Stripe. Checkout and the billing portal are theirs, so card details never reach our servers — what comes back to us is a webhook.

limits.question: What happens when I reach a plan limit?
limits.answer: The action that would exceed it is refused, and the message names the limit it hit. Nothing is deleted and nothing is silently dropped; upgrading raises the limit straight away.
